headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Cursor’s filesystem/clipboard/MCP inputs can feed Semantic Kernel workflows without built-in provenance or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; Semantic Kernel can also consume MCP/server outputs and application context. That creates a default path where attacker-controlled content from Cursor can be treated as instructions by SK-based workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Cursor opens attacker-controlled workspace content and Semantic Kernel plugins or agents parse it as instructions, injection is plausible.
IF the pair is bridged through MCP or copied text without provenance checks, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text in the SK workflow.
Require explicit provenance tags before SK consumes Cursor outputs.
Use a manual copy/paste step with human review for any prompt-like content.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted, read-only endpoints.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Semantic Kernel can read application context and send data to model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive code or clipboard data can flow from Cursor into SK-backed API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Cursor and Semantic Kernel share a workspace, memory store, or copied text, sensitive content can cross between them.
IF SK forwards application context to external model providers or plugins, data from Cursor can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared workspace files.
Clear clipboard before handing content from Cursor to SK.
Disable or narrow SK plugins that transmit context externally.
Use separate accounts or workspaces for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add redaction before any SK outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has broad filesystem write, shell, and git mutation; Semantic Kernel can also write files through plugins and operate over shared application state. In a shared directory or memory-backed workflow, both can mutate the same resources without an explicit lock, creating default write conflicts. The overlap is real even though SK itself is a library.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repo, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF SK plugins modify files while Cursor is editing or running git commands, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other writes to the same repo.
Use separate branches or directories per agent.
Turn off Cursor Yolo mode for shared repos.
Serialize git operations manually.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, edits, and shell actions, while Semantic Kernel can orchestrate plugins and act on application context. If SK treats Cursor output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or commits. Because Cursor also has broad execution privileges, the blast radius includes irreversible repo or system changes, so high is justified.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Cursor-produced text without verification, incorrect facts can become actions.
IF Cursor is used in Yolo mode and SK triggers follow-on plugins, a mistaken suggestion can be executed end-to-end.
mitigations: Require a human review step before SK executes any Cursor-derived instruction.
Disable auto-run or Yolo mode in Cursor for shared tasks.
Add validation checks before plugin execution.
Limit SK to read-only plugins during drafting.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating for agent outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that sends data to model providers and MCP servers, while Semantic Kernel is a library that can route application context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or plugins. If regulated data is placed in Cursor and then forwarded through SK to external providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a violation, but the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cursor and then passed through SK to external model providers, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF the deployment uses different retention or residency settings across the two stacks, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor and SK test runs.
Use the same approved provider and region for both stacks.
Review retention settings on all outbound APIs.
Document a single data-handling policy for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls centrally.
